sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
When Jessica Langerman was 12, she had a favorite TV show.
sentences.zh: 杰西卡·兰格曼12岁时，有一个最喜欢的电视节目。

sentences.en: This is a little embarrassing to admit, but I was crazy about Star Trek.
sentences.zh: 承认这个有点尴尬，但我那时对《星际迷航》着迷得不行。

sentences.en: One day, several of the actors came to my hometown.
sentences.zh: 有一天，几位演员来到了我的家乡。

sentences.en: So I begged my mother to take me, and I walked up to a table, and there was Leonard Nimoy.
sentences.zh: 于是我求妈妈带我去，我走到一张桌子前，莱昂纳德·尼莫伊就在那里。

sentences.en: It was Mr. Spock, the cerebral star of the show, always calm, ever logical.
sentences.zh: 那是斯波克先生，剧中冷静睿智的明星，总是那么沉着，永远充满逻辑。

sentences.en: For years, Jessica had felt a deep kinship with Spock, and now here he was, right in front of her.
sentences.zh: 多年来，杰西卡一直对斯波克有着深深的亲切感，而现在他就在她面前。

sentences.en: And, of course, I knew every angle of his face.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，我熟悉他脸上的每一个角度。

sentences.en: I knew the curve of his ears.
I knew everything about him, or so I felt.
sentences.zh: 我了解关于他的一切，或者我当时是这么觉得的。

sentences.en: And when I put my notebook down for him to autograph, he looked at me with complete blank non-recognition.
sentences.zh: 当我放下笔记本请他签名时，他用一种完全茫然、认不出我的眼神看着我。

sentences.en: And I was so confused in that moment.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我感到无比困惑。

sentences.en: I knew him so well, but he did not know me.
sentences.zh: 我那么了解他，但他却不认识我。

sentences.en: Danny Martinez understands what it's like to feel a deep connection to someone who doesn't know you.
sentences.zh: 丹尼·马丁内斯懂那种对一个不认识你的人产生深厚连接的感觉。

sentences.en: I tell you, I don't get no respect from anyone, you know?
sentences.zh: 跟你说吧，谁都不把我放在眼里，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the last week, my wife, she signed me up for a bridge club.
sentences.zh: 我是说，就在上周，我妻子给我报名参加了一个桥牌俱乐部。

sentences.en: I remember when Rodney Dangerfield died, I cried like I had lost my grandfather.
sentences.zh: 我记得罗德尼·丹杰菲尔德去世时，我哭得就像失去了祖父一样。

sentences.en: And no one could understand why I would care so much.
sentences.zh: 没有人能理解我为什么会在乎那么多。

sentences.en: Eric Palileo says his connection with a singer named Anoni was transformational.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·帕利莱奥说，他与一位名叫安妮的歌手之间的连接具有改变人生的意义。

sentences.en: He still remembers the moment he first heard her song, GhoSt.
sentences.zh: 他还记得第一次听到她的歌《GhoSt》时的情景。

sentences.en: He was 15 at his home in Texas.
sentences.zh: 他当时15岁，在德克萨斯州的家中。

sentences.en: I remember just sitting on the couch and, like, not really knowing even how to react.
sentences.zh: 我只记得自己坐在沙发上，甚至不知道该作何反应。

sentences.en: It's just like a dramatic shift in the way that you're seeing the world.
sentences.zh: 就像是你观察世界的方式发生了戏剧性的转变。

sentences.en: And that couch wasn't just the couch.
sentences.zh: 那张沙发不再只是沙发。

sentences.en: And that room just wasn't just a room.
sentences.zh: 那个房间不再只是房间。

sentences.en: And this house actually had a meaning to it now.
sentences.zh: 这个房子现在对它来说有了真正的意义。

sentences.en: Psychologists sometimes refer to such emotional connections as parasocial relationships.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有时将这种情感连接称为准社会关系。

sentences.en: In some ways, they are akin to the imaginary friends that children have.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它们类似于孩子们拥有的想象中的朋友。

sentences.en: As we grow up, we're told to set such relationships aside.
sentences.zh: 随着我们长大，人们告诉我们要把这种关系放在一边。

sentences.en: To tuck our stuffed animals away in a closet.
sentences.zh: 把我们的毛绒玩具塞进衣柜深处。

sentences.en: Clinging to imaginary companions can suggest that you are lonely or maladjusted.
sentences.zh: 紧抓着想象中的伴侣不放，可能暗示你感到孤独或适应不良。

sentences.en: But what if there is more to these relationships than we realize?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果这些关系不仅仅是我们所意识到的那样呢？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the thin line between the imaginary and the real.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐秘大脑》，探讨想象与现实之间的纤细界限。

sentences.en: Growing up, Meghan Lincoln was different from other kids.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，梅根·林肯与别的孩子不同。

sentences.en: She tried to hide it, but her secret always came out.
sentences.zh: 她试图隐藏这一点，但她的秘密总是藏不住。

sentences.en: Like when her teacher would make everyone go around the room, reading aloud from a book.
sentences.zh: 比如当老师让全班轮流大声朗读书里的内容时。

sentences.en: And then you would read as much as you wanted, and then you would say, done, and then you
sentences.zh: 然后你想读多久就读多久，接着说“读完了”，然后你
会说出另一个人的名字。

sentences.en: And then they would pick up from there.
So that would be the worst experience of my life, because I didn't know when the person
sentences.zh: 所以那将是我生命中最糟糕的经历，因为我不知道那个人什么时候

sentences.en: was going to be done and when my name was going to be called.
sentences.zh: 会读完，什么时候会叫到我的名字。

sentences.en: So I would sit there, trying to figure out how I could get out of the classroom, because
sentences.zh: 所以我只能坐在那里，琢磨着怎么才能溜出教室，因为

sentences.en: She would watch the movie instead of doing the reading, or choose the book that had the
sentences.zh: 她会选择看电影而不是阅读，或者挑选图片最多的

sentences.en: most pictures, or simply figure out a way to get out of the classroom.
sentences.zh: 书，或者干脆想办法离开教室。

sentences.en: When all the other kids were exchanging their homework for another student to grade,
sentences.zh: 当其他孩子都在互相交换作业批改时，

sentences.en: she would raise her hand and say she had to go to the bathroom.
sentences.zh: 她会举手说她得去趟洗手间。

sentences.en: Yeah, I would stay there forever.
I would slowly walk to the bathroom, and then I would hang out there, wash my hands a lot,
sentences.zh: 我会慢吞吞地走到洗手间，然后在里面晃悠，不停地洗手，

sentences.en: look in the mirror, just do whatever I could to waste time.
sentences.zh: 照镜子，只要能消磨时间，什么都做。

sentences.en: But one teacher, Ms. Doyle, noticed Megan getting frustrated when she tried to read.
sentences.zh: 但有一位老师，多伊尔女士，注意到梅根在尝试阅读时感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And so one day she pulled me aside, and we were just talking about life and talking about
sentences.zh: 所以有一天她把我拉到一边，我们聊了生活，聊了

sentences.en: how I was not dumb, really defining dyslexia for me, and then telling me that there were
sentences.zh: 我其实并不笨，真正为我解释了什么是读写困难，然后告诉我，

sentences.en: other people in the world who were dyslexic just like me.
sentences.zh: 世界上还有其他人也和我一样有读写困难。

sentences.en: And, you know, she told me Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她告诉我温斯顿·丘吉尔。
她告诉我沃尔特·迪士尼。

sentences.en: She told me Albert Einstein and Tom Cruise.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦和汤姆·克鲁斯。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, Sonny and Cher.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，索尼与雪儿。
某种东西在梅根的想象中被点燃了。

sentences.en: Cher started popping up in my head all the time.
sentences.zh: 雪儿开始不断地在她脑海中浮现。

sentences.en: I mean, I loved Sonny and Cher.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我喜欢索尼和雪儿。
我喜欢他们的综艺节目。
我有过目不忘的记忆力。

sentences.en: Sonny, you know the only thing wrong with your photographic mind?
sentences.zh: 索尼，你知道你那过目不忘的记忆力唯一的毛病是什么吗？

sentences.en: If you look at Cher and she goes on stage, she's not, quote unquote, your stereotypical
sentences.zh: 如果你看看雪儿，当她走上舞台时，她并不是那种所谓的刻板印象中的
获奖者是因《月满抱佳人》而获奖的雪儿。

sentences.en: She doesn't care if she's wearing this weird old black outfit with, like, you know, where
sentences.zh: 她才不在乎自己是不是穿着那种奇怪的旧黑色衣服，露着大腿，

sentences.en: her thighs are showing and she's got these crazy tights on.
sentences.zh: 还穿着那种疯狂的紧身裤。

sentences.en: She doesn't care what people think about her.
sentences.zh: 她不在乎别人怎么看她。

sentences.en: I want to thank my mom because when I was really young, my mom said, you're not going
sentences.zh: 我要感谢我妈妈，因为当我年纪还小的时候，我妈妈说，你不会是

sentences.en: to be the smartest, you're not going to be the prettiest, you're not going to be the
sentences.zh: 最聪明的，你不会是最漂亮的，你不会是最有才华的，

sentences.en: most talented, but you're going to be special.
And I think as a young girl, not feeling confident of who I was, having someone who was
sentences.zh: 我想作为一个年轻女孩，对自己缺乏自信时，有一个如此坚强的人，

sentences.en: so strong, really made me feel that, why should I care what people are saying about
sentences.zh: 真的让我觉得，我为什么要介意别人在课堂上

sentences.en: One day, the Cher in her mind did something she hadn't done before.
sentences.zh: 有一天，她脑海中的雪儿做了一件以前从未做过的事。

sentences.en: It was her recognizable Cher voice.
sentences.zh: 那是她标志性的雪儿声音。

sentences.en: She was as real to me as my friend next to me.
sentences.zh: 她对我的真实程度，就像我身边的朋友一样。

sentences.en: After this happened a few times, Megan got used to it.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生几次后，梅根就习惯了。

sentences.en: She would only talk to me when I was feeling dumb or insecure.
sentences.zh: 她只在我感到愚笨或缺乏安全感时才会跟我说话。

sentences.en: And if I was feeling like insecure for something that was not school or reading or writing specific,
sentences.zh: 如果是因为学校、阅读或写作之外的事情感到没有安全感，

sentences.en: Now, when Megan's anxiety swirled in, Cher would offer encouragement.
sentences.zh: 每当梅根的焦虑情绪涌上心头时，雪儿就会给予鼓励。

sentences.en: The one thing I always remembered her saying to me is, if you think you are dumb, then you think I am dumb and I am not dumb.
sentences.zh: 我一直记得她对我说的一句话是：如果你觉得自己笨，那你就是觉得我笨，而我可不笨。

sentences.en: And then she would tell me to go back to reading or go back to trying to write something.
sentences.zh: 然后她会叫我回去阅读，或者回去尝试写点东西。

sentences.en: And when she tried to hide out in the bathroom, Cher wouldn't let her.
sentences.zh: 当她试图躲在洗手间里时，雪儿不答应。

sentences.en: I remember her telling me that it was smelly in the bathroom.
sentences.zh: 我记得她告诉我洗手间里有异味。

sentences.en: Why are you sitting in a smelly bathroom?
sentences.zh: 你为什么坐在这个有异味的洗手间里？

sentences.en: She's like, you're better than this.
Go back and take that teSt.
It'll be much better than sitting here in this smelly bathroom.
sentences.zh: 那可比坐在这个臭烘烘的洗手间里强多了。

sentences.en: And I would take my deep breath and I would walk out and I would smile, you know, and I'd probably curse her out a little bit.
sentences.zh: 然后我会深吸一口气，走出去，你知道的，挤出微笑，可能还要在心里小小地咒骂她一下。

sentences.en: And I'd go back into that classroom and take that teSt.
sentences.zh: 接着我会回到教室去参加考试。

sentences.en: After her secret friend helped her for a few years, Megan started to feel more confident.
sentences.zh: 在神秘朋友陪伴了她几年后，梅根开始变得自信起来。

sentences.en: And that's when Cher's voice disappeared.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，雪儿的声音消失了。

sentences.en: It's kind of like Mary Poppins.
sentences.zh: 这有点像《欢乐满人间》里的玛丽·波平斯。

sentences.en: The kids no longer needed her.
Something in my head just told me I didn't need her and she left.
sentences.zh: 我脑海里的某种声音告诉我，我不再需要她了，于是她便离开了。

sentences.en: Maybe she went to some other person's head who needed her.
sentences.zh: 也许她去了另一个需要她的人的脑海里吧。

sentences.en: Today, Megan has multiple degrees, a successful career.
sentences.zh: 如今，梅根拥有多个学位，事业有成。

sentences.en: She's figured out how to manage her dyslexia.
sentences.zh: 她已经找到了应对读写困难的方法。

sentences.en: But she's been reluctant to tell people how Cher helped her.
sentences.zh: 但她一直不太愿意告诉别人雪儿是如何帮助她的。

sentences.en: You know, who has in her voice that sounds like some celebrity?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，谁脑子里会有个听起来像名人的声音？

sentences.en: I just tell people I love her.
sentences.zh: 我只告诉别人我喜欢她。

sentences.en: Megan misses the comfort of Cher's voice.
sentences.zh: 梅根怀念雪儿声音带来的慰藉。

sentences.en: Every now and then, she tries to recreate it.
sentences.zh: 每隔一段时间，她都会试图重现它。

sentences.en: But it's me making her voice.
sentences.zh: 但那是我在模仿她的声音。

sentences.en: I knew it really wasn't her.
But I also didn't feel I was wise enough to be as wise as she was to me.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得当时的自己没有她对我的那样充满智慧。

sentences.en: The voices we hear, the secret friends we have, they often don't seem like mere extensions of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的声音，我们拥有的秘密朋友，它们通常看起来不只是我们自己的延伸。

sentences.en: Megan said Cher seemed to be braver than she was, wiser than she was.
sentences.zh: 梅根说，雪儿似乎比她更勇敢，比她更睿智。

sentences.en: The Cher and Megan's head knew things that Megan didn't know.
sentences.zh: 梅根脑海中的那个雪儿知道一些梅根不知道的事情。

sentences.en: How can one part of the mind know something that another part of the same mind does not know?
sentences.zh: 为什么大脑的一个部分可以知道另一部分却不知道的事情？

sentences.en: When we come back, we explore this question in another domain.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来后，将在另一个领域探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: We look at people who hear not the voice of a singer or a celebrity, but the voice of something much bigger.
sentences.zh: 我们将关注那些听到的不是歌手或名人的声音，而是某种更宏大的声音的人。

sentences.en: I mean, fundamentally, the story of God is a story about the human imagination,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从根本上说，关于上帝的故事是一个关于人类想象力的故事，

sentences.en: the human capacity to take seriously the sense that the world that we see before us is not all there is of the world.
sentences.zh: 是人类认真对待这种观念的能力，即我们眼前看到的世界并不是世界的全部。

sentences.en: As a young person, Tanya Lerman did not believe in God.
sentences.zh: 年轻时的塔尼亚·勒曼并不相信上帝。

sentences.en: I couldn't understand how people could believe in an omnipotent, omniscient maker who would allow people to suffer so much.
sentences.zh: 我不理解人们怎么会相信一个全能、全知的造物主，却又允许人类遭受如此多的苦难。

sentences.en: It seemed logically incoherent to me.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这在逻辑上是讲不通的。

sentences.en: She was known among her peers as an atheiSt.
sentences.zh: 她在同龄人中被称为无神论者。

sentences.en: She even wrote about it in an op-ed for her school newspaper.
sentences.zh: 她甚至在学校校报的专栏文章中写过这一点。

sentences.en: Her friends came up with their own version of the headline.
sentences.zh: 她的朋友们想出了他们自己版本的标题。

sentences.en: The tagline among my friends was that,
sentences.zh: 我朋友之间的一句口头禅是，

sentences.en: Ler person does not believe in God.
sentences.zh: 勒曼这个人不相信上帝。

sentences.en: I mean, I was called Ler person because I was also a feminist and Lerman.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家都叫我“勒曼”，因为我也是个女权主义者，而且姓勒曼。

sentences.en: Anyway, that was the way my friends referred to me.
sentences.zh: 总之，我的朋友们就是这样称呼我的。

sentences.en: Tanya's parents were also actively questioning the idea of religious faith.
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚的父母也曾在积极质疑对宗教信仰的观念。

sentences.en: They had grown up in devout homes.
sentences.zh: 他们都在虔诚的家庭中长大。

sentences.en: Her mother's father was a Baptist minister.
sentences.zh: 她母亲的父亲是一名浸礼会牧师。

sentences.en: Her father's father was a Christian scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 她父亲的父亲是一名基督科学派信徒。

sentences.en: But her father had become a determined atheiSt.
sentences.zh: 但她的父亲成了一个坚定的无神论者。

sentences.en: At one point in college, he actually ceremoniously burnt his membership card to the Mother Church in Boston.
sentences.zh: 在大学的某个时期，他甚至在波士顿隆重地烧掉了他加入基督科学派母教堂的会员卡。

sentences.en: Her mother kept going to church, but loved to read books by Sam Harris, the atheist neuroscientiSt.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲继续去教堂，但喜欢读无神论神经科学家萨姆·哈里斯的书。

sentences.en: You know, my mother also was torn.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我母亲也很纠结。

sentences.en: She just kind of wanted to believe, but it was, she found it logically tough.
sentences.zh: 她只是有点想相信，但她发现这在逻辑上很难做到。

sentences.en: Although her dad disapproved, Tanya's mom took her to church every Sunday.
sentences.zh: 尽管她父亲不赞成，塔尼亚的母亲还是每周日带她去教堂。

sentences.en: Tanya found herself fascinated by how smart, good people could reach very different conclusions about God and religion.
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚发现自己很着迷于那些聪明、善良的人怎么会对上帝和宗教得出如此截然不同的结论。

sentences.en: And I wanted to understand more about how things became real to people and how people came to decide that God was real,
sentences.zh: 我想更多地了解事物是如何对人们变得真实的，以及人们是如何决定上帝是真实的，

sentences.en: how they came to feel that the world was organized in a particular way.
sentences.zh: 他们是如何感觉到这个世界是以某种特定方式组织起来的。

sentences.en: As Tanya grew up, she thought briefly about becoming a psychiatrist, her dad was a psychiatrist, but eventually settled on a different profession, anthropology.
sentences.zh: 随着塔尼亚的长大，她曾短暂地考虑过成为一名精神病医生，她父亲就是精神病医生，但最终她选择了另一个职业——人类学。

sentences.en: If psychiatrists have a set of descriptions about what constitutes normal behavior and assess when and how much people deviate from those norms,
sentences.zh: 如果说精神病医生有一套关于什么是正常行为的描述，并评估人们在什么时候以及在多大程度上偏离了这些规范，

sentences.en: anthropology demands that you suspend judgment, that you try to understand people on their own terms, from the inside out, rather than from the outside in.
sentences.zh: 那么人类学则要求你暂缓判断，试着从当事人的角度、从内到外而不是从外到内去理解他们。

sentences.en: Anthropologists are, in some ways, little amoebas.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，人类学家就像小变形虫。

sentences.en: We're trying to ask what it feels like to live in somebody else's world.
sentences.zh: 我们试图去探究生活在别人的世界里是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And there's an anthropologist called Clifford Gertz who said that before you judge, you need to understand.
sentences.zh: 有一位名叫克利福德·格尔茨的人类学家说过，在评判之前，你需要去理解。

sentences.en: And that that was the kind of the moral impulse of our field.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们这一学科的道德驱动力。

sentences.en: I think the people who become anthropologists want, they're curious about what it's like to walk in someone else's shoes.
sentences.zh: 我认为成为人类学家的人都有这种愿望，他们对体验别人的生活是什么感觉充满好奇。

sentences.en: And I think that you don't do that well if you have a pretty clear view from the outside of what that other world is like.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你从外部对那个异世界有一个相当清晰的看法，你就无法很好地做到这一点。

sentences.en: Tanya realized she was drawn to this approach.
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚意识到自己被这种方法吸引了。

sentences.en: She wanted to immerse herself deeply with people whose frames and norms were different from her own.
sentences.zh: 她想把自己深深地沉浸在那些框架和规范与她不同的人群中。

sentences.en: I mean, at some point, you need to come to a kind of moral reckoning with the world that you are looking at and your sense of who you are in your own world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某个时刻，你需要对你所看到的世界以及你在自己世界中的自我认知进行某种道德上的清算。

sentences.en: But I do think that when you, to the extent that you can, when you let go of who you are and you try to become different, you see and feel things differently.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，当你尽可能地放下自我、试着去成为不同的人时，你对事物的见解和感受也会有所不同。

sentences.en: In the spring of 1983, when she was 23 years old, Tanya decided to put this idea into practice.
sentences.zh: 1983年春天，23岁的塔尼亚决定将这个想法付诸实践。

sentences.en: She was in England, doing her PhD in anthropology.
sentences.zh: 当时她在英国攻读人类学博士学位。

sentences.en: She focused her field research on a group of people who believed they could cast spells and perform magic rituals.
sentences.zh: 她将田野调查的重点放在了一群相信自己能够施咒和举行魔法仪式的人身上。

sentences.en: Tanya, the rationalist, was personally skeptical of these claims, but she had made a commitment to listen openly, without judgment.
sentences.zh: 作为理性主义者的塔尼亚个人对这些说法持怀疑态度，但她已经承诺要以开放的态度去倾听，不做评判。

sentences.en: She attended a retreat with about 50 practitioners at a beautiful, remote manor house.
sentences.zh: 她和大约50名实践者一起参加了一个在美丽而偏远的庄园举办的静修活动。

sentences.en: The leader of the group was Gareth Knight.
sentences.zh: 该团体的领导者是加雷斯·奈特。

sentences.en: To Tanya, he looked like Merlin, the wizard.
sentences.zh: 在塔尼亚看来，他看起来就像巫师梅林。

sentences.en: And he had this big shock of white hair and he had flowing robes.
sentences.zh: 他留着一头蓬松的白发，穿着飘逸的长袍。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, this was Harry Potter land before Harry Potter.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，这就是哈利·波特之前的哈利·波特世界。

sentences.en: The goal of the weekend was to encounter what Gareth called contacts.
sentences.zh: 这个周末的目标是遇到加雷斯所说的“联络人”。

sentences.en: He said contacts were highly evolved human beings, no longer tethered to their bodies, who could offer guidance.
sentences.zh: 他说，联络人是高度进化的人类，不再受肉体束缚，能够提供指导。

sentences.en: They were like wise, invisible people.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是睿智的、看不见的人。

sentences.en: And so he would just talk about them as if they were friends.
sentences.zh: 所以他谈论他们时，就会像他们是朋友一样。

sentences.en: He would, you know, stride up and down before the group of 50 people and talk about, you know, how we're going to do a big ritual event.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他会在那50人面前大步流星地走来走去，谈论诸如我们将如何举行一场盛大的仪式之类的活动。

sentences.en: Gareth explained that he would guide them through a spiritual exercise using a mystical set of pictures.
sentences.zh: 加雷斯解释说，他将带领大家通过一套神秘的图片进行精神锻炼。

sentences.en: A temple, a priestess, a hermit.
sentences.zh: 一座神庙，一位女祭司，一个隐士。

sentences.en: He lit four candles and told everyone to close their eyes.
sentences.zh: 他点燃了四支蜡烛，让每个人闭上眼睛。

sentences.en: They were now aboard a ship, he told them, and they were going to accompany him to another world.
sentences.zh: 他告诉大家，他们现在登上了船，将陪同他前往另一个世界。

sentences.en: And what this man did during the weekend was to, in effect, tell story after story about these pictures in a way that he wanted us to experience these pictures
sentences.zh: 这个人在周末所做的事情，实际上就是讲了一个又一个关于这些图片的故事，他希望我们去体验这些图片，

sentences.en: as if we were living in a dream, as if we were going down a river and we were all in a boat together and we would get out of the boat
sentences.zh: 就好像我们生活在梦中，就好像我们顺流而下，所有人都在同一条船上，然后我们将下船，

sentences.en: and we would look up and we would see a temple and there was the priestess and this is what the priestess looked like.
sentences.zh: 抬头望去，我们会看到一座神庙，女祭司就在那里，这就是女祭司的样子。

sentences.en: And he wanted us to experience those stories as if they were happening.
sentences.zh: 他希望我们去体验这些故事，就好像它们正在发生一样。

sentences.en: Tanya had only planned to record the experiences of the group, but as she imagined the stories along with them
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚原本只打算记录这个团体的经历，但随着她和他们一起想象这些故事，

sentences.en: at that initial retreat and subsequent meetings, she found that her own impressions were becoming a vital source of data.
sentences.zh: 在最初的静修和随后的聚会上，她发现自己的印象正在成为至关重要的第一手数据来源。

sentences.en: Over the first three or four months, it occurred to me that my mental images were becoming sharper, that they were becoming richer.
sentences.zh: 在头三四个月里，我发现我的心智图像变得越来越清晰、越来越丰富。

sentences.en: She started attending the group's weekly dream interpretation class
sentences.zh: 她开始参加该团体的每周梦境解析课，

sentences.en: and she began to keep a dream diary.
And my dreams were becoming vivid and dripping with symbolism.
sentences.zh: 我的梦变得生动起来，并且充满了象征意义。

sentences.en: I remember having this dream at one point in which what I knew was my soul
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次做过这样的梦：我知道那是我的灵魂，

sentences.en: was swimming across a river in a thunderstorm to scramble up the other side on this bank of mud
sentences.zh: 在雷雨中游过一条河，然后爬上另一边的泥泞河岸，

sentences.en: and I kept falling back and then I'd go forward and I remember waking up and thinking,
sentences.zh: 我一次次滑落，然后又往前爬，我记得醒来时我想，

sentences.en: oh my goodness, I'm having different kinds of dreams and that was a dream about my soul.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我正在做不同寻常的梦，那是一个关于我的灵魂的梦。

sentences.en: It was like the work she was doing was changing the way her own mind worked.
sentences.zh: 这就好像她正在做的工作改变了她自己大脑的运作方式。

sentences.en: It was changing what she saw in the world, how she experienced the world.
sentences.zh: 它改变了她在世界上看到的东西，改变了她体验世界的方式。

sentences.en: The world felt as if it was becoming more connected.
sentences.zh: 世界感觉变得更加紧密相连了。

sentences.en: It felt like I was having these synchronicities.
sentences.zh: 感觉我正在经历这些共时性事件。

sentences.en: Things would, you know, I'd walk into the green grocer and the green grocer would say something
sentences.zh: 事情会……你知道的，我走进蔬菜店，蔬菜店老板就会说出

sentences.en: I mean, and so I would have these experiences and over the course of the year,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会经历这些事情，在这一年的时间里，

sentences.en: you know, I really saw myself change, felt myself change.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我真的看到自己发生了变化，感觉自己变了。

sentences.en: When I spoke to her, Tanya thought back to another moment when the line between the real
sentences.zh: 当我与她交谈时，塔尼亚回想起另一个时刻，当时现实与想象之间的界限变得模糊了。
那是她进行田野调查的早期，当时她正坐火车去见加雷斯·奈特。

sentences.en: It was early during her field research and she was on a train to meet Gareth Knight for the first time.
She was reading a book about magic and mysticism.
sentences.zh: 她当时在读一本关于魔法和神秘主义的书。

sentences.en: It was called Experience of the Inner Worlds.
And it was about the experience of power and this idea of a power outside of me that was present
sentences.zh: 这本书讲的是对力量的体验，以及这种存在于世间的、超越自我的力量的观念，

sentences.en: and kind of there in the world.
sentences.zh: 它就那样存在于世界上。

sentences.en: It was kind of new to me.
The book was esoteric and complex and she strained her mind to understand it.
sentences.zh: 这本书既深奥又复杂，她绞尽脑汁去理解它。

sentences.en: On the Kabbalistic Tree of Life framework, we see a method of theosophical classification
sentences.zh: 在卡巴拉生命之树的框架下，我们看到了一种神智学分类方法，

sentences.en: that's able to take in the concept of both creator and the creation.
sentences.zh: 它能够将造物主和造物的概念融合在一起。

sentences.en: This is not so evident in the world.
sentences.zh: 这在世界上并不是那么明显。

sentences.en: And he was talking about Tibetan this and Kabbalistic that and white light that.
sentences.zh: 他在谈论西藏的这个、卡巴拉的那个，还有白光之类的东西。

sentences.en: And I remember kind of just trying to understand the sentences and concentrating so hard and
sentences.zh: 我记得我只是试图去理解这些句子，聚精会神地思考，

sentences.en: there were people around me talking and I was trying to really focus on the book.
sentences.zh: 身边有人在说话，而我正试图专注于这本书。

sentences.en: Right then, she started to feel hot.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，她开始觉得发热。

sentences.en: Like an electrical charge that seemed to move through me, starting above me and moving through my body and going into the floor.
sentences.zh: 就像一股电荷似乎穿过了我的身体，从我头顶上方开始，穿过我的身体，进入了地板。

sentences.en: And it was strong and it was vivid.
It seemed like all of my senses were incredibly sharp.
sentences.zh: 似乎我的所有感官都变得异常敏锐。

sentences.en: And as I was feeling this way, trying to figure out what on earth was going on,
sentences.zh: 正当我这种感觉、试图弄清楚到底发生了什么的时候，

sentences.en: I looked over and there were wisps of smoke coming out of my bag.
sentences.zh: 我转头看去，发现我的包里冒出了一缕缕烟雾。

sentences.en: A battery-powered bike lamp she had stored in her bag was melting.
sentences.zh: 她放在包里的一个电池供电的自行车灯正在融化。

sentences.en: It's like when the battery was melting and there's bicycle lights.
sentences.zh: 这就像电池在融化时，还有自行车灯一样。

sentences.en: Now, there are two ways to think of this.
sentences.zh: 现在，有两种方法来看待这件事。

sentences.en: You can say Tanya's thoughts about power melted the battery.
sentences.zh: 你可以说塔尼亚关于力量的想法融化了电池。

sentences.en: Or you can say, huh, interesting coincidence.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以说，哈，有趣的巧合。

sentences.en: But the point is, if you put yourself in a frame of mind where you expect unusual things to happen,
sentences.zh: 但关键是，如果你让自己处于一种期待不寻常事情发生的精神状态，

sentences.en: you're more likely to see unusual things happen.
sentences.zh: 你就更有可能看到不寻常的事情发生。

sentences.en: The time she spent with Gareth and the others taught Tanya something very important about the imagination.
sentences.zh: 她与加雷斯和其他人共度的时光教会了塔尼亚关于想象力的一个非常重要的道理。

sentences.en: And when you do, remarkable things follow.
sentences.zh: 当你这样做时，非凡的事情就会随之而来。

sentences.en: There's all kinds of things that people experience.
sentences.zh: 人们会体验到各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: But what I can say is that the more time you spend doing what I would call inner sense cultivation,
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，你花在进行我所谓的内在感官培养上的时间越多，

sentences.en: the more likely you are to report these events,
sentences.zh: 你就越有可能报告这些事件，

sentences.en: that people have these moments in which, in effect,
sentences.zh: 人们会经历这样的时刻，即实际上，

sentences.en: what they're imagining breaks forth into the world.
sentences.zh: 他们想象的东西爆发到了现实世界中。
随着她进行更多的研究，

sentences.en: Tanya realized there was a profound disconnect in the way people think about the imagination today
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚意识到，当今人们对想象力的看法与早期人们对它的看法之间存在着深刻的脱节。

sentences.en: and the way they used to think about it in earlier times.
sentences.zh: 我认为，将想象力强调为一种明显非物质的东西，

sentences.en: I think the emphasis on the imagination as something that is obviously not material
sentences.zh: 是随着世俗世界一起出现的，
伴随着这样一种观念：真实的东西就是我们脚下踩的东西，

sentences.en: with a sense that what is real is the stuff that we walk on
sentences.zh: 以及我们看到的、其他人都能看到的东西。

sentences.en: and the things that we see that everybody else can see.
sentences.zh: 而其他的东西则不是那种真正的东西。

sentences.en: And that what is other is not that real stuff.
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚后来成为了斯坦福大学的人类学教授。

sentences.en: Tanya went on to become a professor of anthropology at Stanford University.
sentences.zh: 2002年，她开始了一项新的田野工作，重点关注另一群人，

sentences.en: In 2002, she began some new field work focused on another group of people,
sentences.zh: 即那些想要与上帝建立强烈个人关系的福音派基督徒。

sentences.en: evangelical Christians who wanted to develop an intense personal relationship with God.
sentences.zh: 他们在实践她所说的“内在感官培养”。

sentences.en: They were practicing what she calls inner sense cultivation.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在采访一个年轻的金发南加州女孩，她的头发总是晃来晃去。

sentences.en: And I was interviewing some young, blonde, Southern Californian who's kind of like her hair would swing back and forth.
sentences.zh: 她看起来就像是属于海滩的人。

sentences.en: She looked like she belonged to the beach.
sentences.zh: 我问了她一堆迂腐的问题。

sentences.en: And I was asking her all these pedantic questions.
And at one point she said,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你想了解上帝，就和他一起喝杯咖啡吧。

sentences.en: you know, if you want to understand God, just have a cup of coffee with him.
sentences.zh: 其他人也对她说过类似的话。

sentences.en: Other people told her similar things.
sentences.zh: 在你的生活中让一个抽象的、看不见的实体变得真实的办法，

sentences.en: The way to make an abstract, invisible entity real in your life
sentences.zh: 就是与那个实体去做你对配偶或同事会做的事情。

sentences.en: was to do things with that entity that you would do with a spouse or a co-worker.
sentences.zh: 但人们会说，你需要去了解上帝，

sentences.en: But what people would say is that you needed to get to know God
sentences.zh: 就像你出去和某人喝咖啡时去了解对方一样。

sentences.en: the way you would get to know somebody when you went out for coffee with them.
You became a friend of the person.
You had a back and forth.
You learned to know each other.
You learned to trust each other.
And that that's how you should get to know God.
sentences.zh: 而这就是你们应该如何去认识上帝的方式。

sentences.en: It was like what she had learned in London during the dream sessions some 20 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 这就像她大约20年前在伦敦的梦境体验期间所学到的东西一样。

sentences.en: They're using very similar kinds of what I would call spiritual practices.
sentences.zh: 他们正在使用非常类似我所谓的精神修行的方法。

sentences.en: They were inviting people to use external symbols, props, and internal images, stories,
sentences.zh: 他们邀请人们使用外部符号、道具以及内部的意象、故事，

sentences.en: in order to allow the person to enter a world which is not the world of the day-to-day
sentences.zh: 以便让人们进入一个并非日常生活的世界，

sentences.en: and to come to experience that world as if it is present, as if it's real.
sentences.zh: 并开始体验那个世界，就好像它真的存在、就好像它是真实的一样。

sentences.en: Tanya met people who said they had practiced these techniques so often
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚遇到了一些人，他们说自己经常练习这些技巧，

sentences.en: that they could interact with God as if God was a living, breathing person.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们能够与上帝互动，仿佛上帝是一个活生生、会呼吸的人。

sentences.en: Ever the skeptical scientist, Tanya decided to see if the things she was hearing from evangelical Christians
sentences.zh: 塔尼亚骨子里是个怀疑论科学家，她决定看看自己从福音派基督徒那里听到的这些事情

sentences.en: were reproducible in a scientific experiment.
sentences.zh: 是否能在科学实验中重现。

sentences.en: She randomly assigned some Christians to practice prayer
sentences.zh: 她随机指派了一些基督徒去练习祈祷，

sentences.en: that involved imagining a very intense personal relationship with God.
sentences.zh: 这种祈祷涉及想象与上帝建立一种非常强烈的人际关系。

sentences.en: She had them read a story from the Bible in which Jesus was represented in different forms,
sentences.zh: 她让他们阅读圣经中的一个故事，其中耶稣以不同的形式出现，

sentences.en: for example, as a baby, a shepherd, or on the cross.
sentences.zh: 例如，作为婴儿、牧羊人或在十字架上。

sentences.en: Then she asked subjects to interact with Jesus in their minds,
sentences.zh: 然后她要求受试者在头脑中与耶稣互动，

sentences.en: using all of their senses, sight, sound, smell, touch.
sentences.zh: 调动他们所有的感官：视觉、听觉、嗅觉、触觉。

sentences.en: Here's an example of one set of instructions related to the Bible's 23rd Psalm,
sentences.zh: 这里有一个与圣经《诗篇》第23篇相关的一组指导说明的例子，

sentences.en: Tanya invited the volunteers back after a month.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，塔尼亚邀请志愿者们再次回来。

sentences.en: She asked them what had happened in their minds in the intervening weeks.
sentences.zh: 她询问他们在中间的这几个星期里，脑海中发生了什么。

sentences.en: People in the imaginative prayer group responded very differently
sentences.zh: 进行想象性祈祷组的人们的反应，

sentences.en: than people in the control group.
sentences.zh: 与对照组的人们截然不同。

sentences.en: So I found that people in the prayer group were more likely to say
sentences.zh: 因此我发现，祈祷组的人更有可能说

sentences.en: that their mental images were vivid.
sentences.zh: 他们的心理意象非常生动。

sentences.en: They were more likely to say that God felt more like a person to them,
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能说上帝对他们来说更像一个人，

sentences.en: that they were more likely to have gotten angry at God
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能对上帝生过气，
或者对上帝表现得像是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: They were also more likely to say that they'd had a moment
sentences.zh: 他们也更有可能说自己有过这样的一刻：

sentences.en: when they had heard God speak in a way they could hear with their ears
sentences.zh: 他们听到上帝以一种他们能用耳朵听到声音的方式说话，

sentences.en: or they had seen something that wasn't materially real in the world
sentences.zh: 或者他们看到了世界上物质上并不真实的东西，

sentences.en: or they'd had some vivid sense of God's presence.
sentences.zh: 或者他们对上帝的存在有某种生动的感知。

sentences.en: They were more likely to say that they'd had an experience
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能说自己有过这样一种体验：

sentences.en: as if what had to be experienced in the mind
sentences.zh: 仿佛那些必须在头脑中体验的东西

sentences.en: had somehow broken free and it was experienced with the senses,
sentences.zh: 不知怎么地打破了束缚，并用感官去体验到了，

sentences.en: as if it sort of jumped outside of the mind-world barrier
sentences.zh: 就好像它某种程度上跳出了“头脑-世界”的屏障，

sentences.en: and was felt by them in the world.
sentences.zh: 并且被他们在现实世界中感受到了。

sentences.en: It was like what happened to Megan.
sentences.zh: 这就像梅根身上发生的事情一样。

sentences.en: The Cher she imagined in her mind became Cher.
sentences.zh: 她在脑海中想象的雪儿变成了雪儿。

sentences.en: It was her recognizable Cher voice.
sentences.zh: 那是她那标志性的雪儿的声音。

sentences.en: As people consciously exercised their imaginations,
sentences.zh: 当人们有意识地锻炼他们的想象力时，

sentences.en: their imaginations stopped feeling like imagination.
sentences.zh: 他们的想象力就不再感觉像是想象了。

sentences.en: I would ask people whether God was like an imaginary friend
sentences.zh: 我曾问过人们，上帝是否就像一个想象中的朋友，
